en: Mayon Volcano's perfect cone shape results from alternating eruptions of thick, sticky lava and loose volcanic ash over thousands of years.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River formed because slightly acidic rainwater slowly dissolved the soluble limestone bedrock over millions of years.
The Sierra Madre mountain range blocks moisture from Pacific typhoons, causing the western side of Luzon to experience a dry season.
Tiwi's geothermal power plants generate electricity because underground magma heats groundwater into steam, which then spins giant turbines.
Taal's Main Crater Lake exists because a massive ancient eruption collapsed the volcano's center, creating a deep basin that filled with rain.
The Cagayan River transports eroded soil from the Caraballo Mountains to the sea, gradually building a wide, fertile river delta.
Tubbataha Reefs thrive because the shallow, clear, sunlit waters of the Sulu Sea provide the exact conditions coral polyps need to grow.
Pacific typhoons gain immense strength over the Philippine Sea because warm ocean water evaporates rapidly, feeding massive energy into the storm.
Benguet's rich gold deposits formed when hot, mineral-heavy fluids cooled and crystallized inside the cracks of ancient underground volcanoes.
The Amihan northeast monsoon brings cool, dry weather to the Philippines because it pushes cold air masses down from Siberia.
The Verde Island Passage supports massive marine biodiversity because strong tidal currents constantly mix nutrient-rich waters from the South China Sea and Sibuyan Sea.
The Chico River carved deep canyons through the Cordillera mountains because its fast-flowing water continuously erodes the softer underlying rocks.
